    Now check C3 ($x_0 \lor x_1$): $0 \lor 0 = 0$. **Violates C3.**

    Now check C1 ($x_0 \lor \neg x_3$): $0 \lor \neg x_3 \implies x_3=0$.

    Now check C2 ($x_3 \lor \neg x_1$): $0 \lor \neg 1 \implies 0 \lor F \implies F$. **Violates C2.**

None (The problem has no solution).

The constraints provided in the CNF formula create a logical contradiction regarding the truth values of variables $x(2,0)$, $x(2,1)$, and $x(2,3)$.
